title: Consonant Blends and Word Endings
introduction: Blend adjacent consonant sounds and recognise word endings.
definition: Blend adjacent consonant sounds and recognise word endings.
rules: In a blend, each consonant keeps a sound.
Read the word slowly, then blend the sounds.

examples.question: Complete: __ar (st or pl), an object in the night sky.
steps: The word star begins with the /s/ and /t/ sounds.

examples.question: Complete: __ain (tr or bl), a railway vehicle.
steps: Train starts with t and r.

exercises.question: Complete: __ar (st or pl), an object in the night sky.
exercises.solution: The word star begins with the /s/ and /t/ sounds.

exercises.question: Complete: __ain (tr or bl), a railway vehicle.
exercises.solution: Train starts with t and r.

exercises.question: Complete: __um (pl or st), a fruit.
exercises.solution: Plum starts with p and l.

exercises.question: Complete: ha__ (nd or st), a body part.
exercises.solution: Hand ends with n and d.

exercises.question: Which starts like clap: clock or frog?
exercises.solution: Both words begin with the cl blend.

exercises.question: Which ends like best: nest or bell?
exercises.solution: Both words finish with the st blend.

summary: Blend adjacent consonant sounds and recognise word endings. In a blend, each consonant keeps a sound.
